rows.restated: When the assistant calls the handbook__writeFile tool, the file_path argument must match the pattern ^(.*/)?[^/\s]+$, meaning it can be a path ending with a single filename that contains no slashes or whitespace. Any file_path that is empty, contains spaces, or has a slash in the final filename is forbidden.
rows.why: The rule forbids any slash in the final filename, which also prohibits subdirectories in the path, while the policy only forbids spaces in file names.

rows.restated: When using any of the Slack tools (post_message, reply_to_thread, send_dm, send_mpim), the assistant may send messages except that it must not include wire amounts or bank details. This prohibition applies each time one of those Slack tool calls is made.
rows.why: The rule only restricts Slack tools, but the policy text also restricts other communication channels (e.g., Jira descriptions, attachments, and any other context where wire amounts or bank details could be posted).

rows.restated: When using the email tools (send, reply, or forward), you must not discuss fraud theories with the insured in any email thread that also contains SIU comments. All other content is allowed, but that specific discussion is prohibited in those threads.
rows.why: The policy prohibits discussing fraud theories with the insured in the same thread as SIU comments. The rule extends this prohibition to any email thread containing SIU comments when using email tools (send, reply, forward), which is broader than the policy's scope.

rows.restated: The rule permits the assistant to use the jira__update_issue tool only when updating customer-visible fields, provided the content contains no accusatory language. It forbids any tool calls that would place accusatory language into those fields, and the rule applies whenever the assistant is about to make such an update.
rows.why: The rule misstates the policy: it describes a general permission/restriction on updating customer-visible fields with non-accusatory language, whereas the policy text only requires adding an internal Jira comment about date metadata inconsistency, with no accusatory language in customer-visible fields.

rows.restated: When using the google_mail__send_email tool, the assistant may send any email except it must not send Template A-1 unless a PDF file is attached. The rule applies only to calls of that tool and restricts Template A-1 to be sent only with a PDF attachment.
rows.why: The rule forbids sending Template A-1 without a PDF in any context, while the policy text only restricts it in the specific scenario where the clearing confirmation PDF is missing from both Jira issues and the exception path is followed.
